turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Where is Owen's zero coming from, and who decided it?
I'm not upset, Hale. I'm asking you a question. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in the gradebook?
But I'm not changing the grade.
Then you'll be explaining that to the principal today. On what basis is it staying, Hale? And what, specifically, do you have besides the checker?
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

"Keep going if you like." I'm writing that down, along with the fact that you've shown me nothing. Your own procedure says a parent is contacted before any mark goes in, and nobody called me, so I'm going upstairs unless you give me a reason in the next minute.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.

"The answer is no." That's in my notes, Hale, and I'll want it in an email. Procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern, so a no with nothing behind it is a decision you'll be defending upstairs.
